title: Core: Implement Git change detection
body:
## What I did

Added Git change detection for the ChangeDetectionService so that whenever a new commit is created or the branch is switched, the module graph will be reevaluated. In practice, this means that as soon as file changes are committed, components will no longer be marked "modified".

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Change detection now watches git repository state and automatically rescans (debounced) when refs/HEAD change; detects intent-to-add files so new files are reported correctly.
  * Service can run with change detection disabled and reports readiness as unavailable when so configured.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved watcher lifecycle, reuse and teardown to avoid stray watchers and ensure cleanup on service dispose.
  * More robust handling of worktree/HEAD transitions and watcher errors.

* **Tests**
  * Expanded tests covering git-state subscriptions, debounce behavior, watcher semantics and unsubscribe safety.

comments.body: onGitStateChange() kicks off ensureWatchers() without awaiting it. If a consumer unsubscribes before setupWatchers() finishes, the cleanup runs before watchers exist and the in-flight setup can still create watchers afterward, leaving open FSWatchers with zero callbacks registered. Consider tying cleanup to watcherSetupInFlight (e.g., when the last callback unsubscribes, await/finally the in-flight setup then clearAllWatchers) or re-check callback count immediately before/after each watcher is created.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a race condition between unsubscribe and watcher setup, and suggests tying cleanup to watcherSetupInFlight.

comments.body: getGitDir() assumes <repoRoot>/.git is a directory. In git worktrees/submodules, .git is often a file containing a 'gitdir: …' pointer, so the watcher paths (<repoRoot>/.git/HEAD, etc.) won't exist and commit/branch switching won't be detected. Consider resolving the actual git dir via `git rev-parse --git-dir` (or parsing the .git file) before wiring watchers.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags that .git may be a file in worktrees/submodules and suggests resolving the actual git dir via `git rev-parse --git-dir`.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Potential race condition when unsubscribing during watcher setup.**

If the last callback unsubscribes while `ensureWatchers()` is still in flight, `clearAllWatchers()` may execute before `setupWatchers()` completes, leaving orphaned watchers. The `setupWatchers` method does check `gitStateCallbacks.size === 0` at lines 120-122 and 177-179, which mitigates this partially, but there's still a window where watchers could be created after the check passes.

Consider adding a check in `watchFile` or ensuring `clearAllWatchers` is called after the in-flight setup completes.

<details>
<summary>🛡️ Proposed fix to handle race condition</summary>

```diff
   return () => {
     this.gitStateCallbacks.delete(callback);

     if (this.gitStateCallbacks.size === 0) {
+      // Wait for any in-flight setup to complete before clearing
+      void this.watcherSetupInFlight?.then(() => {
+        if (this.gitStateCallbacks.size === 0) {
+          this.clearAllWatchers();
+        }
+      });
-      this.clearAllWatchers();
     }
   };
```
</details>

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`In Node.js `fs.watch()`, what happens on Linux/macOS when a watched file is atomically replaced or deleted and recreated, and are directory watches recursive for nested paths like `refs/heads/feature/foo`?`

💡 Result:

On Linux and macOS, when a watched file is atomically replaced (e.g., via mv or cp followed by rm, common in editors for safe saves), fs.watch typically emits a 'rename' event for the deletion/removal of the original file (IN_DELETE_SELF or equivalent kqueue event), followed by another 'rename' event for the creation of the new file with the same name. This is because atomic replacement unlinks the original inode and links a new one, appearing as delete then create to the watcher. Subsequent changes to the new file emit 'change' events normally. However, platform differences exist: Linux (inotify) reliably distinguishes metadata/content changes; macOS (kqueue for files, FSEvents for dirs) may emit 'change' for atime updates or coalesce events. Events may be missed or coalesced under rapid operations due to OS buffers. Directory watches with recursive: true (supported on macOS natively via FSEvents, on Linux since Node.js v19.7.0/v18.13.0 via userland traversal) watch all nested paths, including deep ones like refs/heads/feature/foo. The filename in events is relative to the watched directory, so changes deep in subdirs emit with the full relative path (e.g., 'heads/feature/foo'). Non-recursive watches only monitor the top-level directory.

Citations:

- 1: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-01-22-nodejs-watch-file-changes/view
- 2: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/49916
- 3: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/47058
- 4: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/20153244/nodejs-atomic-file-replace-operation-trigger-only-one-time-some-watchers
- 5: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/36005
- 6: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/45098

**Watch parent directories instead of individual Git ref files to avoid inode staleness after atomic replacement.**

Currently, these watches monitor `HEAD`, `packed-refs`, and specific branch ref files individually. Git atomically replaces these files via unlink+rename, which on Linux/macOS causes `fs.watch()` to become bound to the old inode after the first update—subsequent file changes won't trigger callbacks. The fallback to directory watching (line 204) only activates if the initial file watch fails to establish, not if it becomes stale after atomic replacement.

The proactive fix is to watch parent directories (`gitDir` for HEAD/packed-refs, `dirname(branchRef)` for branch refs) and re-read state on events. This avoids both the inode staleness issue and the brittleness of coarse-grained fallbacks like `refs/heads`, which won't catch deeply nested refs like `refs/heads/feature/foo` on non-recursive platforms (though Node.js 22 does support `recursive: true`).

Applies to lines 123-130 and 198-207.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

In `@code/core/src/core-server/change-detection/GitDiffProvider.ts` around lines
123 - 130, The current file watches individual ref files (HEAD, packed-refs,
branch ref files) which breaks when Git atomically replaces files because
fs.watch can stay bound to the old inode; update GitDiffProvider to watch parent
directories instead: replace per-file watches in the block that calls
watchFile(generation, 'head', join(gitDir, 'HEAD'), ...), watchFile(...
'packedRefs', join(gitDir, 'packed-refs'), ...) and the branch-watching logic
inside configureBranchWatcher so they watch gitDir (for HEAD/packed-refs) and
dirname(branchRef) (for branch refs) and on any directory event call
emitGitStateChange() and re-read the specific ref; keep the existing fallback
behavior but prefer directory watches to avoid inode staleness while retaining
re-read semantics used by emitGitStateChange and configureBranchWatcher.
```

</details>
